items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And I’ve seen a video of a show like that in Los Angeles with Ernie Andrews.

ctx.x: Well of course Lester was my Dream Prince of all time. Buck Clayton. I used to say to Harry Lim, “you like Buck Clayton?” “Yeah,” he says “I always remember John Hammond’s line was many times I have heard him but always muted.” So I thought he was married to Singsee, but it seems I think they were just live-in companions for a © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

number of years. She was adorable. And she probably decided she wanted to get married and so she took off with Billy Kyle. I said to Harry Lim, “what do you think Buck Clayton said?” He said, “he probably took his mute out at that point.” I don’t know, I was just crazy about that band. Well there was a period in I guess it was in the 50s when they were playing at Birdland, and it was just like — well it was like going to church, I mean you just went regularly, you know you’d be marked absent if you weren’t there.…
Now he got his start in Chicago, right?
